page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system includes 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor architecture is x86_64, incorporating advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2211.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.45 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly efficient, scoring 2952.0 in Geekbench, which ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core operations, such as software compilation with Clang (21518.0) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (113.07 GB/sec), fall within the average range. For small-model LLM inference (135M), text generation reaches a top-tier speed of 348.03 tokens/sec, while medium-model (7B) text generation operates at an average rate of 16.4 tokens/sec.

The instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options, and GPU-accelerated workloads are not supported. Network bandwidth baseline is rated at 8 Gbps. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.4xlarge offers a dense compute profile with dedicated CPU allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory, making it suitable for compute-bound workloads. Appropriate applications include software compilation, text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, web serving, and lightweight LLM inference.
